title.narrative: Strengthening Resilience of Disaster Affected Communities through Durable Solutions in Oromia and Somali Regions of Ethiopia

description.narrative:
Ethiopia hosts one of the highest numbers of internally displaced persons (IDPs) globally, with 4.51 million identified according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) National Displacement Report 11 published in February 2022. The Federal Government of Ethiopia (GoE) is exerting efforts to advance solutions for internal displacement, including through establishing the Durable Solutions Initiative (DSI) in 2019 designed to provide a principled operational framework for durable solutions and shape multi-sectoral and collective programs of return, relocation, and local integration of IDPs. Somali and Oromia regions, particularly the Harage zones of Oromia Region bordering areas with Somali Region, present priority geographic areas for durable solutions interventions in general.
Considering the complexity and the dimensions of displacement situations in Somali and Oromia regions, this project will pursue a nexus-based multi-dimensional and integrated approach to enable communities to move towards recovery and resilience by employing durable solutions actions that enhance communities’ coping mechanisms against future shocks to anthropogenic disasters and natural hazards. The project will be implemented through the collaborative efforts of three agencies: the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the United Nations Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO), and the United Nations Human Settlements Program (UNHABITAT), to roll out a multi-pillar intervention that aims to take into consideration the diverse aspects of solutions-based programming. The collaboration of the three agencies will ensure synergetic operations and apply integrated approaches to coordinate urban-rural linkages, community cohesion, livelihoods, access to housing, land, and property (HLP), access to basic services, through adequate spatial planning aimed at generating legal, material, and physical protection for displacement-affected communities. The project will ensure that interventions are inclusive of gender, disability, and vulnerability, as well as that they adhere to applicable international human rights standards such as the Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement and stressing the local government on the Kampala Convention (Article IX), which stipulates 1. International organizations and humanitarian agencies shall discharge their obligations under this Convention in conformity with international law and the laws of the country in which they operate. 2. In providing protection and assistance to Internally Displaced Persons, international organizations and humanitarian agencies shall respect the rights of such persons in accordance with international law. 3. International organizations and humanitarian agencies shall be bound by the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence of humanitarian actors, and ensure respect for relevant international standards and codes of conduct as well as Universal Declaration of Human Rights, General Assembly, A/RES/17 A (III), 1948, Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment, General Assembly, A/RES/39/46. 10 December 1984, the Convention on the Rights of the Child and CEDAW among others. Programmatic areas will be interwoven to devise a continuity of care where an area-based approach is adopted with the agencies maximizing resources for a shared group of beneficiaries. The project will target conflict and climate induced IDPs and host communities in various locations of displacement, newly created drought IDPs looking to locally integrate and relocate or return to areas in Fafan and Shabelle zones of Somali Region, and East and West Hararge zones of Oromia Region. These locations have been selected in consideration of i) concentration of returnees, ii) concentration of relocated internally displaced persons (IDPs), iii) concentration of IDPs looking to locally integrate, and iv) anticipation of returnees or relocated persons. The project also aims at responding to the challenges of the disaster risk reduction, that is, internal displacement. The intention is to reduce the impact of existing hardship and increase resilience by supporting the efforts of the government to develop or update existing disaster woreda profile and to enable each woreda to effectively mainstream Disaster Risk Management (DRM) measures in their respective woreda plan. The outcome of this exercise will add to the government risk profile database. To further enhance the objective of the DSI, the project will support the formation, where necessary, and the coordination of Durable Solutions Working Groups (DSWGs) in various regions to assist the regional authorities and stakeholders find solutions to internal displacement caused by conflict and natural disasters. Displacement affects women differently than men, and it differs at different stages of a crisis. Changes in gender roles are accelerated
